content:
Former Legislative Council member Wong Kam-fai is charged with dangerous driving and other offences, and is currently on bail awaiting trial. He served as a legislator from December 2022 to July of this year. According to a review of Legislative Council records by *The Collective*, during his tenure of over 42 months, his office's total operating expenses exceeded HK$10 million, including over HK$1.5 million in consultancy fees. He successively hired Chan Tak-ming, president, and Ng Hok-ling, vice president, of the "Hong Kong Guangdong Innovation and Technology Association" — which he himself founded — as consultants. Chan Tak-ming has been continuously employed since January 2023, receiving HK$20,000 to HK$30,000 per month, totalling over HK$1 million in consultancy fees. According to the guidelines for Legislative Council members applying for reimbursement of operating expenses, "a member should not engage as consultants his political party or any organisation over which his political party has financial interests or control." Is there any issue with hiring key personnel from connected organisations as paid consultants? The Legislative Council Secretariat replied to *The Collective*'s inquiry stating that the guidelines have already been set out and it would not provide further comments. Wong Kam-fai, who has no political affiliations, responded by saying that the association operates on a voluntary basis as a non-profit organisation. In addition, towards the end of his first term, Wong Kam-fai also distributed bonuses to his office staff, with total employee expenses declared to the Legislative Council that month exceeding HK$773,000.

Office operating expenses during tenure exceeded HK$10 million

According to *The Collective*'s review of Wong Kam-fai's "reimbursement for office operating expenses" in the Seventh Legislative Council, the amounts ranged from approximately HK$2.877 million to HK$2.984 million annually. From October 2025 onwards, in the Eighth Legislative Council, the amount was increased to HK$3.02 million. During Wong's 42 months in office, he declared office operating expenses exceeding HK$10 million to the Legislative Council. In 2023 and 2024, his declared expenses were approximately HK$1.876 million and HK$2.89 million respectively.

However, in 2025, Wong's declared expenses reached HK$4.006 million. The increase was attributable to staff expenses rising from HK$2.24 million the previous year to HK$3.215 million; consultancy fees also rose from HK$480,000 to HK$640,000, among other items. After Wong was re-elected in 2026, his expenses from January to June totalled HK$1.413 million.

Over HK$1 million spent hiring executives of his own association as legislative consultants

A review of records shows that from February 2023 to June 2026, Wong Kam-fai declared consultancy fees exceeding HK$1.5 million to the Legislative Council. During the 36 months from 2023 to 2025, he continuously engaged Chan Tak-ming, president of the "Hong Kong Guangdong Innovation and Technology Association," at HK$30,000 per month, spending HK$1.08 million. After Wong was re-elected in the current term until his resignation, he continued to engage Chan for six months at HK$20,000 per month, spending HK$120,000 in total. The "Hong Kong Guangdong Innovation and Technology Association" was founded by Wong Kam-fai in 2016, and he has served as its executive president.

Three consultancy tender submissions — two from bidders who were association members

As early as March 2023, Wong submitted tender documents to the Legislative Council. At the time, the three consultancy bids came from Tai Ching-fung, Chan Tak-ming, and Cheng Kwok-wai. Both Tai and Chan were members of the "Hong Kong Guangdong Innovation and Technology Association," with Tai serving as head of the finance group. Tai's quotation was HK$45,000, Cheng's was HK$35,000, and Chan's was the lowest at HK$30,000. Chan ultimately secured the consultancy.

The tender description indicated that Chan's consultancy work involved assisting with advocacy and planning on innovation and technology, education, various social policies and issues; facilitating communication and interaction across sectors; and assisting with regional office operations.

Hiring the association's vice president as a consultant — with only one quotation submitted

Wong also engaged Ng Hok-ling, vice president of the association, as a consultant. Ng has served as Wong's consultant on innovation and technology and education policy since June 2023, receiving a consultancy fee of HK$5,000 in the first month and HK$10,000 per month thereafter, totalling HK$315,000. Only one quotation was submitted for Ng's consultancy. Regarding the tender scope, Wong stated that Ng "is equally proficient in both innovation and technology and education policies," "can respond quickly to work requirements with a flexible service format, and the quality of his service meets the needs of my parliamentary work."

Legislative Council guidelines: Should not engage political party-controlled organisations as consultants

According to Section 24 of the Legislative Council's "Guidelines for Members Applying for Reimbursement of Operating Expenses," "A member should not engage as consultants his political party or any company/organisation over which his political party has financial interests or control." Wong Kam-fai, who has no political affiliations: Association operates as a non-profit

When *The Collective* inquired with Wong Kam-fai as to whether engaging key personnel from connected organisations as consultants might conflict with the guidelines, Wong replied that Chan Tak-ming's role covers district and political liaison, while Ng Hok-ling's covers education. Wong stated that the association was founded by a group of like-minded innovation and technology professionals hoping to contribute to the development of Hong Kong and Mainland innovation and technology. "We are all volunteers, and the association has always operated on a non-profit basis." A review of records shows Wong has no political affiliations.

Office chief received HK$276,000 in salary upon contract completion

Apart from consultancy expenses, regarding the remuneration of legislative assistants, records show that upon completing his term in 2025, Wong declared two items of staff expenses totalling over HK$773,000 to the Legislative Council, of which approximately HK$423,000 covered paid leave, together with November and December salaries.

Wong also distributed approximately HK$350,000 in bonuses to five office staff members. The office chief received a monthly salary of HK$63,500; upon her contract expiring in December, she received compensation for accrued annual leave, together with approximately HK$181,000 in salaries for two months, plus a bonus equivalent to 1.5 months' salary of HK$95,200, totalling HK$276,000. The other four received bonuses equivalent to 2.5 months' salary from Wong, ranging from HK$54,000 to HK$75,000.

Legislative Council Secretariat: Guidelines for reimbursement of operating expenses have been set out

*The Collective* previously inquired with the Legislative Council Secretariat as to whether Wong's practices of hiring the president and vice president of his own association as long-term consultants and distributing bonuses were appropriate. The Secretariat replied that the relevant details were already set out in the guidelines for Legislative Council members applying for reimbursement of operating expenses and it would not provide further comments.

"Guidelines for Legislative Council Members Applying for Reimbursement of Operating Expenses" — Guiding Principles (partial) ・Members or their relatives must not have any direct or indirect financial interests in transactions involving applications for reimbursement. ・Members should avoid applying for reimbursement for any transactions that might lead the public to believe that the member, their relatives, or business partners would benefit. ・Members should adhere to the principles of openness, fairness, and accountability when using public funds. ・Where conflicts of interest are unavoidable or have already arisen, members should declare their interests when applying for reimbursement, with declarations being available for public inspection. ・If a transaction for which reimbursement is or may be applied for gives rise to a suspicion of conflict of interest, the member should handle such matters in accordance with the principle of public interest. ・Members should as far as possible separate their private and Legislative Council affairs/interests, and make known to the public that they have done so, to avoid giving rise to a suspicion of conflict of interest or the pursuit of improper private gain.

Guidelines on the Use of Consultancy Services by Legislative Council Members: Members may engage consultants on a permanent or non-permanent basis. To avoid conflicts of interest, the following requirements must be complied with: ・A separate contract should be signed with each engaged consultant. ・The contract should clearly set out the scope of services to be provided by the consultant. ・The name of the consultant and the fees charged should be listed on the reimbursement claim form for public inspection. ・A copy of the contract should be submitted to the Secretariat (contracts are not required to be available for public inspection). ・Members or their relatives should not have any interest relationship with engaged consultants. ・Members should not engage as consultants their political party or any company/organisation over which their political party has financial interests or control.

In the declaration records, Wong Kam-fai classified the bonus amounts under "other," noting that no bonuses had been disbursed during the first three years of his term, and that the arrangement was discretionary, "and therefore not specified in the contract." He also stated that the team had jointly promoted and implemented various bills, motions, and initiatives, and that "after careful consideration of the office's financial position, I have decided to award the following staff members a bonus in recognition of their hard work and contributions during the Seventh Legislative Council term." A review of the "Guidelines for Applying for Reimbursement of Operating Expenses" shows that members may set aside funds within the operating expenses reimbursement amounts to cover staff contractual bonuses, double pay, or end-of-contract gratuities, etc. The amount of set-aside funds should be determined according to the signed contract and other legal responsibilities, and should not be excessive. Members may receive disbursed funds without the need to submit supporting documents.

On 29 June this year, Wong Kam-fai was arrested by police on suspicion of four offences including drink driving and careless driving after allegedly hitting two vehicles on the CUHK campus and fleeing the scene. When the case was exposed by the media on 1 July, Wong had not yet declared it to the Legislative Council, and attended the Handover anniversary reception as usual to take photos, until 3 July, when Wong resigned from all his positions in the Legislative Council.

Apart from being a member of the Election Committee constituency in the Legislative Council, Wong also serves as a member of the 14th National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, and Associate Dean (External Affairs) of the Faculty of Engineering at CUHK. Following the drink driving incident, CUHK announced the suspension of his administrative duties until now. In September this year, police formally charged him with four offences including "dangerous driving." He was granted bail, and the case was adjourned to 11 November for mention.

Wong Kam-fai drink driving | Arrested for "careless driving" and other offences, formally charged with four offences including "dangerous driving," first court appearance on 9 September.

Wong Kam-fai drink driving | Legislative Council: handling seriously; review of records: four offences carry maximum penalty of imprisonment. Wong Kam-fai drink driving | Accused of hitting two vehicles and fleeing the scene, arrested on four offences; after the incident was exposed, expressed regret over "a traffic incident." Was convicted of drink driving 11 years ago and had licence suspended.
